record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates dialog-model metrics at several parameter counts, testing scale-related performance trends with measures different from held-out cross-entropy loss.
record.gate_note: The study reports measurements for six foundation metrics at 2B, 8B, and 137B parameters, and discusses their trends with size. It does not report held-out pretraining loss, fitted power laws, extrapolation predictions, or a compute-optimal allocation. The single 137B FT quality-safety result is not a size-scaling result and is not included as a row.
record.test_reason: Reports dialog downstream metrics (crowdworker-rated quality, safety, groundedness) for 2B, 8B and 137B models, pre-trained and fine-tuned. This bears on whether downstream performance improves with scale (V6) in a new setting, open-domain dialog. There is no loss, fit or allocation result, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say scaling alone improves pre-trained quality and groundedness/informativeness but does not improve safety much, and that fine-tuning gives large gains on all metrics. Their conclusion phrases it as scaling improving all metrics, with safety and groundedness still far behind human levels. They fit no scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies model size and evaluates dialog quality, safety, and groundedness metrics rather than measuring held-out cross-entropy loss or fitting scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling outcomes differ by metric and training treatment: pre-training-only safety changes little, and some fine-tuned metrics are not monotonic across sizes.
record.problems: The scaling evaluation reports only three model sizes and point estimates without uncertainty measures. It does not fit a curve or test predictive accuracy; some metric trends are weak or non-monotonic. The paper notes that its example domain transcripts are cherry-picked.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying size-scaling metric rows were left out. The single FT quality-safety (137B) entry in Table 28 was excluded because it is not part of a size comparison.

untested.parts: 'Predictably': no curve is fitted and no prediction of a larger model is tested. There are only three sizes and no relation to pretraining loss. The scaling is confounded with different step counts (501k, 521k, 3M), so it is not pure parameter scaling.

record.verdict_notes: All row values match Table 28. The reader's supports label wrongly included the PT specificity rows r4–r6, which are flat from 2B to 8B; these are moved to limits_scope. Section 7 contains a qualitative, unfitted remark that a PT model 'multiple orders of magnitude larger' than 137B might be needed to reach LaMDA's 92.3% sensibleness. It implies slow returns to scale on that metric but is not a measured result. The FT quality-safety (137B) and PALMS toxicity comparisons are not size comparisons and were rightly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law fit over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of much larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Fine-tuned models are evaluated, but the study does not test whether a power-law form holds for fine-tuning or other training regimes.
The study evaluates dialog foundation metrics across three sizes, not a broad set of downstream tasks or performance as a function of pretraining loss; it does not fit a predictive relationship.
No comparison of fitting methods, parameter-counting choices, training schedules, or scaling-law exponents.

relationships.condition: PT sensibleness, interestingness, groundedness, informativeness; LaMDA (fine-tuned) sensibleness, specificity, groundedness, informativeness across 2B/8B/137B
relationships.reason: Each metric rises monotonically with size, e.g. PT groundedness 45→47.1→57.9 and LaMDA informativeness 41.8→50.2→62.3 (r1-r3, r7-r9, r13-r18, r19-r24, r31-r36).
relationships.display_finding: Each specified metric increased monotonically, including pretrained groundedness from 45 to 47.1 to 57.9 and fine-tuned informativeness from 41.8 to 50.2 to 62.3.

relationships.condition: PT safety, PT specificity, LaMDA interestingness and LaMDA safety
relationships.reason: PT safety rises only 84.8→88, which the authors say does not benefit much from scaling. PT specificity is flat from 2B to 8B. LaMDA interestingness and safety are non-monotonic (r4-r6, r10-r12, r25-r30).
relationships.display_finding: Pretrained safety rises only from 84.8 to 88 and specificity stays flat from 2B to 8B, while LaMDA interestingness and safety vary non-monotonically.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: PT and LaMDA quality, groundedness, and informativeness metrics across 2B, 8B, and 137B
reader_labels.reason: Most of these metrics rise with size; the authors also state that quality generally improves with model size and groundedness improves as model size increases (r1-r9, r13-r18, r19-r24, r31-r36).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: PT safety and LaMDA interestingness and safety across the reported sizes
reader_labels.reason: PT safety changes little with size, while LaMDA interestingness and safety are not monotonic across all three sizes (r10-r12, r25-r30).
